part: Page composition, Admin (13), Sources / Source registry
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/screens/13-admin.png (the artboard's own TIER column and tab row); the operator's /admin layout fix, 2026-09-08, items 3, 4 and 6
notes: The Source registry sub-tab has NO artboard of its own: artboard 13 draws the Provisional review state (compose-13-admin measures that one). This spec measures the region the operator's report was about, and it exists because nothing measured it before: the registry body rendered five loose blocks straight into the content column (a 'Source Intelligence' h2, the B.2 progress card, a full-width orange scraping box, a 'Source Tiers, how we rank authority' explainer, a T1-T7 summary card strip) and at 1024 that strip overflowed the column by 336px and painted under the rail.

Item 3 is a REMOVAL and a re-shape. Artboard 13 makes tier a COLUMN in the source table, not a card set, so the T1-T7 cards and the explainer go. The vocabulary lands in three places, all reachable by vertical scroll or Tab, per the operator's absolute rule that nothing may require a horizontal reach: the header legend (a square per tier, its authority label as tooltip and accessible name), a 'Tier definitions' overlay carrying the full lines, and the per-tier COUNTS in the table's facet row, where clicking one filters the table.

The facet is built from the filter mechanism that already existed and had never been mounted: `sourceStore.toggleTierFilter` + `filterSources`, which has always matched on `effective_tier ?? base_tier`. The counts are derived through that same key (`facetTierOf`), so a chip can never name a number its own click would not return. Nothing new was invented to hold the counts.

Item 4 pulls the other three regions in: the h2 + subtitle became the card head (title and count), B.2 became the neutral regeneration state-note strip under the tab row (its 'By format / By priority / Tag coverage / Recent' placeholder columns are gone), and the orange scraping box became the Action-band state-note strip at the card foot with Cadence / Save / Emergency stop as its 44px action row. Both strips are the SHARED StateNote, the same part the provisional card's pipeline note uses; there is no second strip component.

The card's view tab row uses TabRow's PAGE placement inside the card's own 16px inset rather than the card-head placement artboard 13 gives the provisional row. The card-head placement never wraps, which is right for that artboard's five tabs on one line at 1440 and wrong for these seven views: measured 938px of tabs in a 764px card, i.e. a horizontal scroller, which is exactly what the operator's accessibility rule forbids. Wrapping keeps every view reachable.

The scraping strip is NOT asserted here: `GlobalPauseToggle` renders nothing until /api/admin/sources/pause-global answers, and this sandbox has no live Supabase project (DEVIATION-LOG.md). Its structure is measured by eye in the built screenshots; a row that would report NOT BUILT against a correct component is a false finding, not a strict check (CLAUDE.md rule 14).

region 1b, the count sits in the header right (item 4: no separate h2 outside a card)
region 2, the tier legend is in the card header, one square per tier
children.note: SEVEN, not the operator's eight: the source tier vocabulary is T1-T7 (src/lib/tier-labels.ts, the SoT under the tier-labels drift guard). Logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md rather than an eighth square invented to match the count in the instruction.

region 3, the regeneration state note sits under the card's tab row
region 3a, it is the shared StateNote in its neutral variant, not a second strip
region 4, the tier counts live in the facet row, one chip per tier
region 4a, each facet chip states its own live count

forbid.reason: The operator's accessibility rule, which is wider than this page: nothing in the product may require an arrow button to scroll horizontally to reach it.

forbid.name: no Export queue control
forbid.reason: Item 5 builds it only if an export-queue function exists. Re-grepped src/app/api and src/lib this lane: the only hits are bulk-import's CSV PARSER, spec09's CSV UPLOAD contract and `parseCsvFilter` query-string helpers. Nothing exports a queue, so the button is not drawn (ruling 1.1) and is logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md.
